title: CarbTune Pro redesign foundation and dynamic tuning architecture
scope: Translate the approved CarbTune redesign into an implementation-ready product architecture, preserve the proven CT-0060 data/history foundation, establish the new visual system, define the knowledge graph and dynamic tuning stack, and prepare the codebase for a controlled implementation without inheriting the Build 51 form-wizard workflow.
objectives: Implement the approved professional dark-shell/light-work-surface visual direction as the canonical design system.
Replace page-click progression with evidence- and verification-driven workflow state.
Define static Pages 1-5, Dynamic Tuning Stack, Job Overview, and Customer Report as the product workflow.
Formalize the CarbTune knowledge graph, dependency/invalidation rules, provenance, freeze points, anti-loop behavior, and sweet-zone logic.
Preserve Vehicle Records, immutable job/configuration history, migration, audit foundations, and other validated CT-0060 infrastructure.
Create an internal Knowledge Graph Inspector specification for development and diagnostic QA.
constraints: Do not merge redesign work to main until acceptance criteria pass and the redesigned workflow is reviewable.
Do not preserve Build 51 behavior merely for visual compatibility; the blueprint is authoritative for workflow behavior.
Do not invent vehicle facts, specifications, component identity, test results, or manufacturer data.
Technicians enter facts; CarbTune owns issue state, progression state, invalidation, prioritization, and stopping logic.
Unverified required evidence may block progression; verified abnormal evidence must generate diagnostic work rather than block Page 5 completion.
No generic universal carburetor checklist where component-specific logic is available.
Do not destroy or silently rewrite historical evidence. Corrections append provenance-aware history.
Retain local-first compatibility during this phase; no fake backend or premature production database migration.

visualContract.shell: dark charcoal/black top bar and left navigation
visualContract.workspace: warm white/light gray central technician work sheet with subtle stacked-sheet depth

semanticColors.red: actual fault, unsafe condition, hard stop

visualContract.style: professional shop diagnostic software; restrained, spacious, strong typography hierarchy, minimal decorative cards/borders, no glowing AI motifs or chat-first presentation
visualContract.navigation: persistent vehicle/RO strip plus left job index showing Pages 1-5, generated Stack sheets, Overview, and Report

acceptanceTests.expected: The canonical blueprint, knowledge graph, and implementation contract are present and internally consistent.
A technician cannot manually force diagnostic/progression states; state changes derive from evidence and rules.
Page 5 can complete with verified abnormal data but cannot complete with required unverified data.
Dynamic Stack sheets follow OBJECTIVE -> EVIDENCE -> ACTION -> VERIFICATION -> OUTCOME and are generated from current dependencies/evidence rather than a fixed page list.
Changing a dependency invalidates only affected conclusions and can generate new verification work without rewriting prior history.
The redesigned shell and working pages match the approved dark-shell/light-sheet visual direction on phone, tablet, and desktop.
Existing CT-0059/CT-0060 vehicle, job, migration, validation-lifecycle, snapshot, and history behavior remains intact unless explicitly superseded by the new contract.
Automated QA detects orphan knowledge nodes, dead-end paths, circular diagnostic loops, missing verification, unsupported numeric recommendations, and unsafe test-path eligibility.

implementationNotes: Design work is isolated on branch design/knowledge-graph-v1.
The user delegated product-design and implementation-detail decisions to ChatGPT/Astra, with the approved generated-screen visual direction treated as the reference aesthetic.
Major product decisions should be encoded in durable repository documents rather than left only in conversation history.
Implementation should proceed in large coherent batches once the architecture contract for that batch is sufficiently specified.

validation.summary: CT-0061 has entered active design; implementation validation has not begun.
